note: San Francisco traffic-signal poles, mast arms and head mounts, modelled in code from the dimensions of Caltrans RSP ES-7C (sources) and the game's signal-hardware constants (props-js.json.gz), with modelling values where no sheet was read (modellingValues). No third-party geometry or image is used: the maps are baked and weathered by the script. Frames: glTF Y up; a pole's origin at its foot on its axis, its arm side +X (the handhole at -X); an arm part's origin on the arm axis, +X along the arm (armTube unit length, scaled to the arm); a mount's origin on the pole (or arm) axis at the head's centre (the arm), +X toward the head. Every part in two finishes (finishes): painted and galvanised; their level 0 files differ (the maps), the far levels are shared.

modellingValues.heavyHexNut: ASME B18.2.2 heavy hex nut proportions: across flats 1.5 x the bolt + 1/8 in, height ~ the bolt
modellingValues.washer: ASTM F436 washer proportions: outside diameter 2 x the bolt, 5/32 in thick
modellingValues.levellingGap: the base plate on levelling nuts, the gap left open (no grout), as the reference photographs show
modellingValues.handhole: 4 x 7 in opening in a raised 3/4 in frame, centre 19 in over the plate (mast); 2 1/2 x 5 in on the posts
modellingValues.poleCap: cast cap 3/8 in over the shaft, domed
modellingValues.pedestalPipe: 4 in nominal steel pipe (4.5 in outside diameter) on a cast flared base, as San Francisco pedestal posts
modellingValues.armRadii: the arm tube as the game built it in code (eo-render props_lib: radius 0.09 m at the pole to 0.06 m at the end; ES-7C gives 7 to 8 in at the pole)
modellingValues.mountPipe: 1 1/2 in nominal pipe (1.9 in outside diameter) bracket arms, as Caltrans side-mount signal brackets; a pedestrian head standing off its pole on two such arms (pedReach) from its clamshell
modellingValues.weathering: paint fade, dust, chips, rust and grime amounts are artistic, matched by eye to the reference photographs
modellingValues.armTaper: the rising arms lose 0.14 in of outside diameter per foot of length from ES-7E's diameter at the pole (a common tapered steel arm taper; no sheet read gives it)
modellingValues.armLevelDiameter: a level arm takes ES-7E's minimum outside diameter at the pole for its length class and the rising arms' taper: the sheet's diameter is the arm's strength for its length and loads, rise or none (no SFMTA arm drawing was read)
modellingValues.armRiseShape: the arm's axis at rise * (1 - (1 - t)^p) over its root, p = tan(angle at the pole) * E / rise (at least 1): it leaves the pole at ES-7E's angle and ends level, as the sheet draws the arm curving
modellingValues.nameSignHang: a Street Name sign hangs level 6 cm under the arm's lower end over its width, in the longest stretch of the arm free of the heads, on two flat bars 15 cm in from its ends (no SF mounting detail read)
modellingValues.pushButton: an accessible push button unit after the San Francisco installations' look: a housing 12 x 16 x 6.6 cm, a 5 cm button with a raised arrow, on a channel clamped to the pole by two bands, the sign over it (sizes are modelling values)
modellingValues.mastCut: the mast pole split at 2.0 m and 4.45 m over its foot (its shaft's uv column edges): the foot holds the base plate, bolts, weld and handhole, the top the upper shaft and the cap; a pole of another height draws the shaft between at its own length
modellingValues.pushButtonSign: the R10-3e(CA) face drawn here after CA MUTCD 2026 Figure 2B-27(CA) (p. 273) in Overpass: panel layout, legends and the arrow as the figure has them, the symbols simple shapes; not the official artwork
modellingValues.cabinetPad: the cabinet stands on a cast concrete pad 3 in over the sidewalk, 6 cm wider than the cabinet all round, its top edge eased (no SFMTA or Caltrans foundation sheet was read)
modellingValues.cabinetDetail: the MSF60's two doors raised 4 mm on its front with a 14 mm seam, a latch handle and lock each by the seam, three hinges on each outer edge, a louvred intake at each door's foot, a police panel door on the right door, a hood overhanging 25 to 35 mm with a drip lip, a base flange; the shell mill-finish aluminium gone dull, rain-streaked under the hood, splashed at the foot, with graffiti painted out in mismatched grey patches and sticker residue as the city's cabinets carry (artistic amounts)
modellingValues.pullBoxLegend: the No. 5 lid of precast concrete, flush with the sidewalk, cast with TRAFFIC SIGNAL along its length (1 1/4 in letters) and two 1/2 x 2 in lifting slots; the box's top wall round it
modellingValues.signChannel: two aluminium channels (1 1/2 in web, 3/4 in flanges, 0.09 in thick) across the back of an arm's Street Name sign at a quarter of its height from top and bottom, as the reference photographs show on San Francisco sign backs (Lombard and Hyde); no SFMTA sign detail was read
